sanskrit: manyunā hi samāviṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavās te 'mitaujasaḥ dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇāṃ sabhāṃ nītāṃ dharmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm
english: For the Pandavas, those of immeasurable might, were seized with rage upon seeing Krishnaa — their lawful wife, that glorious lady — dragged into the assembly hall.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanasya tā vācaḥ śrutvā te dāruṇodayāḥ karṇasya ca mahārāja na svapsyantīti me matiḥ
english: Having heard those terrible words spoken by Duhshasana and by Karna, O great king, it is my conviction that they will not sleep peacefully.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ hi te mahārāja yathā pārthena saṃyuge ekādaśatanuḥ sthāṇur dhanuṣā paritoṣitaḥ
english: For you have heard, O great king, how the eleven-formed Shiva — the Immovable One — was gratified by Partha's bow in battle.

sanskrit: kairātaṃ veṣam āsthāya yodhayām āsa phalgunam jijñāsuḥ sarvadeveśaḥ kapardī bhagavān svayam
english: The lord of all the gods himself, the braid-haired Bhagavan, wishing to test him, assumed the guise of a Kirata mountaineer and fought with Phalguna.

sanskrit: tatrainaṃ lokapālās te darśayām āsur arjunam astrahetoḥ parākrāntaṃ tapasā kauravarṣabham
english: Then those world-guardians revealed themselves to Arjuna — that bull of the Kauravas who had striven with ascetic power — for the purpose of granting him celestial weapons.

sanskrit: naitad utsahate 'nyo hi labdhum anyatra phalgunāt sākṣād darśanam eteṣām īśvarāṇāṃ naro bhuvi
english: No other man on earth is capable of obtaining the direct vision of these divine lords — none other than Phalguna.

sanskrit: maheśvareṇa yo rājan na jīrṇo grastamūrtimān kas tam utsahate vīraṃ yuddhe jarayituṃ pumān
english: O king, that hero whose body, though seized, was not worn down by Maheshvara himself — what man is capable of exhausting him in battle?

sanskrit: āsāditam idaṃ ghoraṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam draupadīṃ parikarṣadbhiḥ kopayadbhiś ca pāṇḍavān
english: This dreadful, tumultuous, hair-raising situation was brought about by those who dragged Draupadi about and provoked the Pandavas to fury.

sanskrit: yatra visphuramāṇoṣṭho bhīmaḥ prāha vaco mahat dṛṣṭvā duryodhanenorū draupadyā darśitāv ubhau
english: Therein, with quivering lips, Bhima uttered his great vow upon seeing Duryodhana display both his thighs to Draupadi.

sanskrit: ūrū bhetsyāmi te pāpa gadayā vajrakalpayā trayodaśānāṃ varṣāṇām ante durdyūtadevinaḥ
english: "I shall shatter your thighs, O wretch, with my thunderbolt-like mace at the end of thirteen years — you who played that wicked game of dice."

sanskrit: sarve praharatāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ sarve cāmitatejasaḥ sarve sarvāstravidvāṃso devair api sudurjayāḥ
english: They are all foremost among warriors, all of immeasurable energy, all masters of every weapon, and even the gods find them exceedingly difficult to overcome.

sanskrit: manye manyusamuddhūtāḥ putrāṇāṃ tava saṃyuge antaṃ pārthāḥ kariṣyanti vīryāmarṣasamanvitāḥ
english: I believe that the Parthas, blazing with wrath, filled with valor and indignation, will bring your sons to their end in battle.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kiṃ kṛtaṃ sūta karṇena vadatā paruṣaṃ vacaḥ paryāptaṃ vairam etāvad yat kṛṣṇā sā sabhāṃ gatā
english: Dhritarashtra said: What has Karna achieved, O charioteer, by speaking those harsh words? Enmity enough already exists from the fact that Krishnaa was brought into the assembly hall.

sanskrit: apīdānīṃ mama sutās tiṣṭheran mandacetasaḥ yeṣāṃ bhrātā gurur jyeṣṭho vinaye nāvatiṣṭhate
english: Will my sons of dull intellect stand firm now — they whose elder brother, their elder and guide, does not abide by proper conduct?

sanskrit: mamāpi vacanaṃ sūta na śuśrūṣati mandabhāk dṛṣṭvā māṃ cakṣuṣā hīnaṃ nirviceṣṭam acetanam
english: Even my counsel, O charioteer, that dull-witted one does not heed, seeing me bereft of sight, motionless, and as though without consciousness.

sanskrit: ye cāsya sacivā mandāḥ karṇasaubalakādayaḥ te 'py asya bhūyaso doṣān vardhayanti vicetasaḥ
english: And his dull counselors — Karna, Shakuni and the rest — those men of confused understanding, only increase his faults further.

sanskrit: svairamuktā api śarāḥ pārthenāmitatejasā nirdaheyur mama sutān kiṃ punar manyuneritāḥ
english: Even arrows loosely shot by Partha of immeasurable energy would burn down my sons — how much more so those impelled by rage?

sanskrit: pārthabāhubalotsṛṣṭā mahācāpaviniḥsṛtāḥ divyāstramantramuditāḥ sādayeyuḥ surān api
english: Arrows hurled by the strength of Partha's arms, discharged from his great bow, and empowered by the mantras of celestial weapons, could lay low even the gods.

sanskrit: yasya mantrī ca goptā ca suhṛc caiva janārdanaḥ haris trailokyanāthaḥ sa kiṃ nu tasya na nirjitam
english: He whose counselor, protector, and friend is Janardana — Hari, the lord of the three worlds — what indeed has he not conquered?

sanskrit: idaṃ ca sumahac citram arjunasyeha saṃjaya mahādevena bāhubhyāṃ yat sameta iti śrutiḥ
english: And this too is a most wonderful marvel concerning Arjuna, O Sanjaya — so the tradition tells — that he came to grips with Mahadeva himself, arm to arm.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ sarvalokasya khāṇḍave yatkṛtaṃ purā phalgunena sahāyārthe vahner dāmodareṇa ca
english: And what was done long ago in the Khandava forest before the eyes of all the world by Phalguna, together with Damodara, for the sake of helping Agni —

sanskrit: sarvathā nāsti me putraḥ sāmātyaḥ sahabāndhavaḥ kruddhe pārthe ca bhīme ca vāsudeve ca sātvate
english: — in every way my son has no hope — not with his ministers, not with his kinsmen — when Partha, Bhima, Vasudeva, and the Satvata are enraged.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca yad idaṃ śocitaṃ rājñā dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa vai mune pravrājya pāṇḍavān vīrān sarvam etan nirarthakam
english: Janamejaya said: O sage, this lamentation of King Dhritarashtra — having already sent the heroic Pandavas into exile — is entirely futile.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi rājā putraṃ svam upekṣetālpacetasam duryodhanaṃ pāṇḍuputrān kopayānaṃ mahārathān
english: For how could a king neglect his own son of mean understanding — Duryodhana — who was provoking those great chariot warriors, the sons of Pandu?

sanskrit: kim āsīt pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ vane bhojanam ucyatām vāneyam atha vā kṛṣṭam etad ākhyātu me bhavān
english: What was the food of the sons of Pandu in the forest — please tell me: was it forest-gathered, or was it cultivated grain? Let your honor recount this.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vāneyaṃ ca mṛgāṃś caiva śuddhair bāṇair nipātitān brāhmaṇānāṃ nivedyāgram abhuñjan puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: Those bulls among men ate forest produce and deer brought down by pure arrows, first offering the food to the brahmanas before eating it themselves.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu śūrān maheṣvāsāṃs tadā nivasato vane anvayur brāhmaṇā rājan sāgnayo 'nagnayas tathā
english: Those valiant great bowmen dwelling in the forest were followed, O king, by brahmanas both with their sacred fires and without.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ sahasrāṇi snātakānāṃ mahātmanām daśa mokṣavidāṃ tadvad yān bibharti yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Thousands of brahmanas who were graduates of sacred learning, great-souled, and ten thousand likewise who were versed in the knowledge of liberation — all these Yudhishthira sustained.

sanskrit: rurūn kṛṣṇamṛgāṃś caiva medhyāṃś cānyān vanecarān bāṇair unmathya vidhivad brāhmaṇebhyo nyavedayat
english: He slew black deer, rurupastures, and other fit forest animals with arrows, and duly offered them to the brahmanas in the prescribed manner.

sanskrit: na tatra kaś cid durvarṇo vyādhito vāpy adṛśyata kṛśo vā durbalo vāpi dīno bhīto 'pi vā naraḥ
english: There, no man was seen with a sickly complexion or afflicted by disease, nor thin or weak, nor wretched or fearful.

sanskrit: putrān iva priyāñ jñātīn bhrātṝn iva sahodarān pupoṣa kauravaśreṣṭho dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: The foremost of the Kauravas, Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, cherished them as beloved sons, as kinsmen, as own-born brothers.

sanskrit: patīṃś ca draupadī sarvān dvijāṃś caiva yaśasvinī māteva bhojayitvāgre śiṣṭam āhārayat tadā
english: And the glorious Draupadi, having fed all her husbands and all the twice-born first, like a mother, would then herself eat what remained.

sanskrit: prācīṃ rājā dakṣiṇāṃ bhīmaseno; yamau pratīcīm atha vāpy udīcīm dhanurdharā māṃsahetor mṛgāṇāṃ; kṣayaṃ cakrur nityam evopagamya
english: The king hunted in the east and Bhimasena in the south; the twins in the west and north — those bowmen ranging daily in pursuit of deer for meat brought great slaughter.

sanskrit: tathā teṣāṃ vasatāṃ kāmyake vai; vihīnānām arjunenotsukānām pañcaiva varṣāṇi tadā vyatīyur; adhīyatāṃ japatāṃ juhvatāṃ ca
english: And so, while they dwelt in the Kamyaka forest — longing anxiously for Arjuna, bereft of him — five full years passed by, as they studied, recited prayers, and performed oblations.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sudīrgham uṣṇaṃ niḥśvasya dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ abravīt saṃjayaṃ sūtam āmantrya bharatarṣabha
english: Vaishampayana said: Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, heaving a long and hot sigh, summoned Sanjaya the charioteer and spoke to him, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: devaputrau mahābhāgau devarājasamadyutī nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca pāṇḍavau yuddhadurmadau
english: Nakula and Sahadeva — those two sons of the divine Ashvins, those two greatly blessed Pandavas, of radiance equal to the king of the gods — are fierce and intoxicated in battle.

sanskrit: dṛḍhāyudhau dūrapātau yuddhe ca kṛtaniścayau śīghrahastau dṛḍhakrodhau nityayuktau tarasvinau
english: They are firm-weaponed, of far-striking range, resolute in battle, quick of hand, of firm wrath, ever ready, and swift in action.

sanskrit: bhīmārjunau purodhāya yadā tau raṇamūrdhani sthāsyete siṃhavikrāntāv aśvināv iva duḥsahau na śeṣam iha paśyāmi tadā sainyasya saṃjaya
english: When those two — Bhima and Arjuna — stand at the forefront of battle, striding like lions, as irresistible as the twin Ashvins, I see no remnant of my army left then, O Sanjaya.

sanskrit: tau hy apratirathau yuddhe devaputrau mahārathau draupadyās taṃ parikleśaṃ na kṣaṃsyete tv amarṣiṇau
english: For those two, who are peerless on the chariot in battle, those two great chariot warriors who are sons of the gods, burning with indignation, will not forgive that torment inflicted on Draupadi.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇayo vā maheṣvāsā pāñcālā vā mahaujasaḥ yudhi satyābhisaṃdhena vāsudevena rakṣitāḥ pradhakṣyanti raṇe pārthāḥ putrāṇāṃ mama vāhinīm
english: Whether the great bowmen of the Vrishnis or the mighty Panchalas — protected in battle by Vasudeva who is true to his word — the Parthas will burn down my sons' army in combat.

sanskrit: rāmakṛṣṇapraṇītānāṃ vṛṣṇīnāṃ sūtanandana na śakyaḥ sahituṃ vegaḥ parvatair api saṃyuge
english: O son of a charioteer, the onslaught of the Vrishnis led by Rama and Krishna cannot be withstood even by mountains in battle.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye maheṣvāso bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ śaikyayā vīraghātinyā gadayā vicariṣyati
english: In the midst of them, the great bowman Bhima of terrible prowess will range about with his iron mace that slays heroes.

sanskrit: tathā gāṇḍīvanirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ gadāvegaṃ ca bhīmasya nālaṃ soḍhuṃ narādhipāḥ
english: Likewise, the twang of the Gandiva — like the crack of a thunderbolt — and the force of Bhima's mace: no lords of men are capable of enduring them.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ suhṛdāṃ vāco duryodhanavaśānugaḥ smaraṇīyāḥ smariṣyāmi mayā yā na kṛtāḥ purā
english: Then I, who have followed in Duryodhana's wake, will recall — too late — the words of friends that I should have heeded and acted upon before.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vyatikramo 'yaṃ sumahāṃs tvayā rājann upekṣitaḥ samarthenāpi yan mohāt putras te na nivāritaḥ
english: Sanjaya said: This is a very great transgression that you have let pass, O king — that through delusion your son was not restrained, even though you had the power to do so.

sanskrit: śrutvā hi nirjitān dyūte pāṇḍavān madhusūdanaḥ tvaritaḥ kāmyake pārthān samabhāvayad acyutaḥ
english: For upon hearing that the Pandavas had been defeated at dice, Madhusudana — the infallible Achyuta — hastened to Kamyaka to visit the Parthas.

sanskrit: drupadasya tathā putrā dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ virāṭo dhṛṣṭaketuś ca kekayāś ca mahārathāḥ
english: Likewise the sons of Drupada headed by Dhrishtadyumna, and Virata, and Dhrishtaketu, and the Kekayas — all great chariot warriors.

sanskrit: taiś ca yat kathitaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā pārthān parājitān cāreṇa viditaṃ sarvaṃ tan mayā veditaṃ ca te
english: And all that was spoken by them upon seeing the defeated Parthas — all of it was learned by me through spies, and I have informed you of it.

sanskrit: samāgamya vṛtas tatra pāṇḍavair madhusūdanaḥ sārathye phalgunasyājau tathety āha ca tān hariḥ
english: There, after meeting the Pandavas, Madhusudana pledged himself to be Phalguna's charioteer in battle, and Hari said to them: "So be it."

sanskrit: amarṣito hi kṛṣṇo 'pi dṛṣṭvā pārthāṃs tathāgatān kṛṣṇājinottarāsaṅgān abravīc ca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: For Krishna too was filled with indignation upon seeing the Parthas reduced to such a condition — wearing black deer-skins as upper garments — and he spoke to Yudhishthira.

sanskrit: yā sā samṛddhiḥ pārthānām indraprasthe babhūva ha rājasūye mayā dṛṣṭā nṛpair anyaiḥ sudurlabhā
english: "That prosperity of the Parthas which existed at Indraprastha during the Rajasuya sacrifice — which I witnessed, unmatched by other kings —

sanskrit: yatra sarvān mahīpālāñ śastratejobhayārditān savaṅgāṅgān sapauṇḍroḍrān sacoladraviḍāndhakān
english: "— where I saw all the rulers of the earth, terror-struck by the might of weapons, along with the Vangas, Angas, Paundras, Odras, Colas, Dravidas, and Andhakas —

sanskrit: sāgarānūpagāṃś caiva ye ca pattanavāsinaḥ siṃhalān barbarān mlecchān ye ca jāṅgalavāsinaḥ
english: "— and those who dwell along the ocean coast, and those who inhabit cities, the Sinhalas, Barbaras, Mlecchas, and those who dwell in the arid lands —

sanskrit: paścimāni ca rājyāni śataśaḥ sāgarāntikān pahlavān daradān sarvān kirātān yavanāñ śakān
english: "— and the western kingdoms by the hundreds down to the sea-shore, the Pahlavas, the Daradas, all the Kiratas, the Yavanas, and the Shakas —

sanskrit: hārahūṇāṃś ca cīnāṃś ca tukhārān saindhavāṃs tathā jāguḍān ramaṭhān muṇḍān strīrājyān atha taṅgaṇān
english: "— the Harahunasand Chinas, the Tukharas, the Saindhavas, the Jagudas, the Ramathas, the Mundas, the kingdoms of women, and the Tanganas —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo ye ca te bharatarṣabha āgatān aham adrākṣaṃ yajñe te pariveṣakān
english: "— these and many others, O bull of the Bharatas, I saw arrive as tributaries at your sacrifice —

sanskrit: sā te samṛddhir yair āttā capalā pratisāriṇī ādāya jīvitaṃ teṣām āhariṣyāmi tām aham
english: "— that prosperity of yours which those fickle and treacherous men have seized — taking their lives in return, I shall recover it for you."

sanskrit: rāmeṇa saha kauravya bhīmārjunayamais tathā akrūragadasāmbaiś ca pradyumnenāhukena ca dhṛṣṭadyumnena vīreṇa śiśupālātmajena ca
english: "Together with Rama, O descendant of Kuru, and with Bhima, Arjuna, and the twins, and with Akrura, Gada, Samba, and Pradyumna, and with Ahuka, and with the hero Dhrishtadyumna, and with the son of Shishupala —

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ raṇe hatvā sadyaḥ karṇaṃ ca bhārata duḥśāsanaṃ saubaleyaṃ yaś cānyaḥ pratiyotsyate
english: "— having slain Duryodhana in battle forthwith, and Karna, O Bharata, and Duhshasana and the son of Subala, and whoever else shall oppose us —

sanskrit: tatas tvaṃ hāstinapure bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito vasan dhārtarāṣṭrīṃ śriyaṃ prāpya praśādhi pṛthivīm imām
english: "— then you, dwelling in Hastinapura together with your brothers, having obtained the sovereignty of the Dhartarashtras, shall govern this earth."

sanskrit: athainam abravīd rājā tasmin vīrasamāgame śṛṇvatsu teṣu sarveṣu dhṛṣṭadyumnamukheṣu ca
english: Then the king spoke to him in that assembly of heroes, while all of them were listening — those headed by Dhrishtadyumna.

sanskrit: pratigṛhṇāmi te vācaṃ satyām etāṃ janārdana amitrān me mahābāho sānubandhān haniṣyasi
english: "I accept your true word, O Janardana; O mighty-armed one, you shall slay my enemies together with their allies."

sanskrit: varṣāt trayodaśād ūrdhvaṃ satyaṃ māṃ kuru keśava pratijñāto vane vāso rājamadhye mayā hy ayam
english: "After the completion of thirteen years, make your word true, O Keshava; for this exile in the forest has been pledged by me in the assembly of kings."

sanskrit: tad dharmarājavacanaṃ pratiśrutya sabhāsadaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogās te śamayām āsur añjasā keśavaṃ madhurair vākyaiḥ kālayuktair amarṣitam
english: Having heard those words of Dharmaraja, the assembly members headed by Dhrishtadyumna straightway pacified the enraged Keshava with sweet words suited to the occasion.

sanskrit: pāñcālīṃ cāhur akliṣṭāṃ vāsudevasya śṛṇvataḥ duryodhanas tava krodhād devi tyakṣyati jīvitam pratijānīma te satyaṃ mā śuco varavarṇini
english: And they spoke to the unsullied Panchali while Vasudeva listened: "Duryodhana shall forfeit his life through your anger, O goddess; we pledge you this truthfully — weep not, O you of lovely complexion."

sanskrit: ye sma te kupitāṃ kṛṣṇe dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ prāhasaṃs tadā māṃsāni teṣāṃ khādanto hasiṣyanti mṛgadvijāḥ
english: "Those who laughed at you, O Krishna, when they saw you enraged — beasts and birds shall laugh in turn while eating their flesh."

sanskrit: pāsyanti rudhiraṃ teṣāṃ gṛdhrā gomāyavas tathā uttamāṅgāni karṣanto yais tvaṃ kṛṣṭā sabhātale
english: "Vultures and jackals shall drink their blood, dragging away their heads — the heads of those who dragged you along the floor of the assembly hall."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ drakṣyasi pāñcāli gātrāṇi pṛthivītale kravyādaiḥ kṛṣyamāṇāni bhakṣyamāṇāni cāsakṛt
english: "You shall see, O Panchali, the limbs of those men dragged across the earth and devoured again and again by flesh-eating creatures."

sanskrit: parikliṣṭāsi yais tatra yaiś cāpi samupekṣitā teṣām utkṛttaśirasāṃ bhūmiḥ pāsyati śoṇitam
english: "The earth shall drink the blood of those — their heads severed — who tormented you then, and of those also who looked on in indifference."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhā vācas tadocuḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ sarve tejasvinaḥ śūrāḥ sarve cāhatalakṣaṇāḥ
english: Thus spoke those bulls among men in many various words — all of them radiant, all warriors, all bearing the marks of the unvanquished.

sanskrit: te dharmarājena vṛtā varṣād ūrdhvaṃ trayodaśāt puraskṛtyopayāsyanti vāsudevaṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Those great chariot warriors, chosen by Dharmaraja, after the completion of thirteen years shall march forth with Vasudeva at their head.

sanskrit: rāmaś ca kṛṣṇaś ca dhanaṃjayaś ca; pradyumnasāmbau yuyudhānabhīmau mādrīsutau kekayarājaputrāḥ; pāñcālaputrāḥ saha dharmarājñā
english: Rama and Krishna and Dhananjaya, Pradyumna and Samba, Yuyudhana and Bhima, the sons of Madri, the sons of the Kekaya king, the sons of Panchala — together with Dharmaraja.

sanskrit: etān sarvāṃl lokavīrān ajeyān; mahātmanaḥ sānubandhān sasainyān ko jīvitārthī samare pratyudīyāt; kruddhān siṃhān kesariṇo yathaiva
english: Who, wishing to preserve his life, would rise to oppose in battle all these heroes of the world, these invincible great-souled ones with their allies and armies — enraged as they are, like maned lions?

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yan mābravīd viduro dyūtakāle; tvaṃ pāṇḍavāñ jeṣyasi cen narendra dhruvaṃ kurūṇām ayam antakālo; mahābhayo bhavitā śoṇitaughaḥ
english: Dhritarashtra said: What Vidura told me at the time of the dice game — "If you defeat the Pandavas, O king, this is certainly the end-time of the Kurus; there will be a great fear, a flood of blood" —

sanskrit: manye tathā tad bhaviteti sūta; yathā kṣattā prāha vacaḥ purā mām asaṃśayaṃ bhavitā yuddham etad; gate kāle pāṇḍavānāṃ yathoktam
english: — I believe that will indeed come to pass, O charioteer, just as Kshattar spoke those words to me before. Without doubt this war will happen when the time of the Pandavas has expired, as was foretold.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca astrahetor gate pārthe śakralokaṃ mahātmani yudhiṣṭhiraprabhṛtayaḥ kim akurvanta pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: When the great-souled Partha had gone to the realm of Shakra for the purpose of obtaining weapons, what did the Pandavas headed by Yudhishthira do?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca astrahetor gate pārthe śakralokaṃ mahātmani nyavasan kṛṣṇayā sārdhaṃ kāmyake puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: When the great-souled Partha had gone to the realm of Shakra for the purpose of obtaining weapons, those bulls among men continued to dwell at Kamyaka together with Krishnaa.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid ekānte vivikta iva śādvale duḥkhārtā bharataśreṣṭhā niṣeduḥ saha kṛṣṇayā dhanaṃjayaṃ śocamānāḥ sāśrukaṇṭhāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ
english: Then one day, in a secluded and solitary place, in a grassy spot, those best of the Bharatas sat down in grief together with Krishnaa, lamenting for Dhananjaya, their throats choked with tears, deeply sorrowful.

sanskrit: tad viyogād dhi tān sarvāñ śokaḥ samabhipupluve dhanaṃjayaviyogāc ca rājyanāśāc ca duḥkhitāḥ
english: Grief overwhelmed them all on account of that separation — afflicted by the loss of Dhananjaya and by the loss of their kingdom.

sanskrit: atha bhīmo mahābāhur yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata nideśāt te mahārāja gato 'sau puruṣarṣabhaḥ arjunaḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ yasmin prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: Then Bhima of mighty arms spoke to Yudhishthira: "At your command, O great king, that bull among men has gone — Arjuna, in whom the vital breath of the sons of Pandu is established."
